A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adjoint Sampling. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-energy sampling and molecular conformer-generation experiments, with additional ablations and runtime analyses in Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains original sampling experiments and appendix analyses, including revised SPICE and GEOM-DRUGS conformer-generation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the Reciprocal Adjoint Matching objective, replay-buffer procedure, geometric extensions, and pretraining method remain unchanged. Expanded fixed-point explanations and references to earlier code do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55, and molecular conformer generation on SPICE and GEOM-DRUGS. Dataset subsets used for energy-model accuracy evaluation also remain unchanged. Sample-selection corrections do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal comparators—PIS, DDS, LogVariance, iDEM variants, and RDKit ETKDG—remain. However, Table 4 removes the MACE-versus-eSEN conformer-generation comparison on GEOM-DRUGS while retaining it on SPICE.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the stated SPICE test size from 100 to 80 molecules, and Figure 8 removes the 1–2-rotatable-bond groups. Since v1's Appendix G already specified 80 molecules with 3–10 rotatable bonds, this establishes a reported-setting correction rather than proving that the evaluation cohort changed.

E4.justification: Appendix H.3 narrows evidence about robustness to the energy-function choice: Table 4 retains SPICE results but removes GEOM-DRUGS results. Reciprocal-projection ablations, runtime analysis, energy histograms, and threshold analyses remain.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged, including standard deviations across test molecules in the conformer tables. Revised deviation values do not introduce a new statistical procedure; no new repeated-run counts or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: The central conformer comparison in Table 2 is substantially revised. For example, unrelaxed Cartesian GEOM-DRUGS precision coverage changes from 41.19% to 28.44%, with AMR changing from 1.46 to 1.86. Figures 4 and 12 also change, and Table 4 loses its GEOM-DRUGS results. Synthetic results in Table 1 remain identical. The PDFs do not fully explain the revised results, preventing attribution to same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds explicit fixed-point equations and a general conditional future-cost definition including the running cost f (v3 Equations 34–36), extending the earlier sampling-specific presentation. The principal reciprocal-projection results and their Appendix C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient on-policy sampling, stochastic-control guarantees, geometric structure, and scalable amortized molecular conformer generation.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a substantive explanation distinguishing current-control expectations and moving regression targets from PDDS/TSM. Appendix F.2 removes the asserted memoryless-noise-schedule requirement while retaining the Dirac initialization. Table 4 also drops the interpretation that eSEN generalizes slightly better to GEOM.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit code/benchmark and model links, discloses exclusion of 30 additional SPICE training molecules, and identifies Tables 4–5 as experiments using earlier code. Architecture and hyperparameter descriptions otherwise remain stable; the underlying code changes are unspecified.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands to NETS, LEAPS, additional GFlowNet and stochastic-control work, and more bridge-matching references. The relationship to PDDS/TSM is explained more explicitly, but the paper's overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized expansions and rewrites affect Sections 3.1–3.2, related work, and Appendix A.2, alongside dataset-description corrections. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several appendix plots are redrawn or resized, and figures and tables are regrouped nearer their discussions. Figure 8 removes two bond-count categories, Table 4 loses its GEOM-DRUGS columns, and captions gain clarifications. The overall visual design and figure/table inventory remain stable.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility through explicit resource links, clearer fixed-point and prior-work explanations, correction of the main-text SPICE test count, and disclosure of older-code experiments. These gains are limited by removal of GEOM-DRUGS energy-choice evidence and insufficient explanation of the revised Table 2 scores. The revision supports a limited quality improvement rather than stronger evidence of methodological superiority.
